name: LINCKS
tagline: Linköping University's early-1990s object-centred, versioned multi-user database for shared documents.
description: LINCKS was a research database system from the IISLAB group at Linköping University's Department of Computer and Information Science, built to explore intelligent information systems. It stored small, semi-structured information chunks (each with a structured part for AI processing and a free-form part for users) that combine into composite objects shared by many users for different purposes, with alternative views over the same data, a full database history, notification of parallel edits and a hypertext-like X11 interface. Version 2 was released publicly over FTP under the GNU license in September 1993, with 2.2 patch level 1 following in June 1994, for SunOS, Solaris and other Unix systems. It has long been inactive and is of historical interest.
statusNote: Research prototype (Linköping University); public releases 1993-1994 and no development since the mid-1990s.
strengths: Composite objects built from shared, semi-structured chunks
Full database history and alternative views over the same information
Notification when several users edit related objects in parallel
Early example of hypertext-style browsing of a shared database
weaknesses: Research prototype from the early 1990s, long unmaintained
useCases: Studying early versioned, semi-structured and hypertext databases
